description: First slice of LLVM IR transformation passes. Each entry is a concise transformation-rule spec (Phase 3 of LLVM_LEARNING.md) that compiles via domains/llvm_pass_compiler.py:install_transformation_rule into a substrate-native RewriteRule.
source: LLVM_LEARNING.md Phase 3; LangRef instruction semantics for the predicates.

passes.name: constfold_add
passes.doc: add(c1, c2) where both are integer constants → fold to c1 + c2. Replaces every use of the add's result with the new constant, deletes the add.

passes.name: constfold_sub
passes.doc: sub(c1, c2) where both are integer constants → fold to c1 - c2.

passes.name: constfold_mul
passes.doc: mul(c1, c2) where both are integer constants → fold to c1 * c2.

passes.name: identity_add_zero_right
passes.doc: add X, 0 → X. The zero constant on the right is the additive identity; the result is just X.

passes.name: identity_add_zero_left
passes.doc: add 0, X → X. Symmetric to identity_add_zero_right.

passes.name: identity_mul_one_right
passes.doc: mul X, 1 → X. The one constant on the right is the multiplicative identity.

passes.name: identity_mul_zero_right
passes.doc: mul X, 0 → 0. The zero absorbs the product; the result is the zero constant.

passes.name: identity_sub_self
passes.doc: sub X, X → 0. Subtracting a value from itself is the zero constant.

passes.name: identity_sub_zero
passes.doc: sub X, 0 → X. Subtracting zero is the additive identity.

passes.name: identity_mul_one_left
passes.doc: mul 1, X → X. Symmetric to identity_mul_one_right.

passes.name: identity_mul_zero_left
passes.doc: mul 0, X → 0. Symmetric to identity_mul_zero_right.

passes.name: identity_and_self
passes.doc: and X, X → X. Bitwise AND is idempotent on identical operands.

passes.name: identity_or_self
passes.doc: or X, X → X. Bitwise OR is idempotent on identical operands.

passes.name: identity_and_zero_right
passes.doc: and X, 0 → 0. Zero absorbs bitwise AND.

passes.name: identity_and_zero_left
passes.doc: and 0, X → 0. Symmetric to identity_and_zero_right.

passes.name: identity_or_zero_right
passes.doc: or X, 0 → X. Zero is the bitwise-OR identity.

passes.name: identity_or_zero_left
passes.doc: or 0, X → X. Symmetric to identity_or_zero_right.

passes.name: identity_xor_self
passes.doc: xor X, X → 0. Bitwise XOR of identical operands is zero.

passes.name: identity_xor_zero_right
passes.doc: xor X, 0 → X. Zero is the bitwise-XOR identity.

passes.name: identity_xor_zero_left
passes.doc: xor 0, X → X. Symmetric to identity_xor_zero_right.

passes.name: identity_shl_zero
passes.doc: shl X, 0 → X. Shifting left by zero bits is the identity.

passes.name: identity_lshr_zero
passes.doc: lshr X, 0 → X. Logical shift right by zero bits is the identity.

passes.name: identity_ashr_zero
passes.doc: ashr X, 0 → X. Arithmetic shift right by zero bits is the identity.

passes.name: constfold_and
passes.doc: and(c1, c2) where both are integer constants → fold to c1 & c2.

passes.name: constfold_or
passes.doc: or(c1, c2) where both are integer constants → fold to c1 | c2.

passes.name: constfold_xor
passes.doc: xor(c1, c2) where both are integer constants → fold to c1 ^ c2.

passes.name: constfold_shl
passes.doc: shl(c1, c2) where both are integer constants → fold to c1 << c2. b ∉ [0,63] → 0 (substrate convention; LLVM defines as poison).

passes.name: constfold_lshr
passes.doc: lshr(c1, c2) where both are integer constants → fold to (unsigned)c1 >> c2. Logical shift fills with zeros.

passes.name: constfold_ashr
passes.doc: ashr(c1, c2) where both are integer constants → fold to c1 >> c2 (sign-extending). Arithmetic shift preserves the sign bit.

passes.name: dce_add
passes.doc: Pure add with no uses → delete. Add is side-effect-free; if no instruction consumes its result, removing it preserves observable behavior.

passes.name: dce_sub
passes.doc: Pure sub with no uses → delete.

passes.name: dce_mul
passes.doc: Pure mul with no uses → delete.

passes.name: dce_and
passes.doc: Pure and with no uses → delete.

passes.name: dce_or
passes.doc: Pure or with no uses → delete.

passes.name: dce_xor
passes.doc: Pure xor with no uses → delete.

passes.name: dce_shl
passes.doc: Pure shl with no uses → delete.

passes.name: dce_lshr
passes.doc: Pure lshr with no uses → delete.

passes.name: dce_ashr
passes.doc: Pure ashr with no uses → delete.

passes.name: strength_reduce_mul_by_2
passes.doc: mul X, 2 → shl X, 1. Multiplication by 2 lowers to single-cycle shift-left — same value, cheaper to execute on every modern ISA.

passes.name: strength_reduce_mul_by_4
passes.doc: mul X, 4 → shl X, 2.

passes.name: strength_reduce_mul_by_8
passes.doc: mul X, 8 → shl X, 3.

passes.name: strength_reduce_mul_by_16
passes.doc: mul X, 16 → shl X, 4.

passes.name: cse_add
passes.doc: Common subexpression elimination for add. Two add instructions with the same operands produce the same value — keep one, rewire uses of the other to it, delete the duplicate.

passes.name: cse_sub
passes.doc: CSE for sub.

passes.name: cse_mul
passes.doc: CSE for mul.

passes.name: cse_and
passes.doc: CSE for bitwise and.

passes.name: cse_or
passes.doc: CSE for bitwise or.

passes.name: cse_xor
passes.doc: CSE for bitwise xor.

passes.name: reassoc_add
passes.doc: (a + b) + c → a + (b + c). Right-associate chains of pure-binary adds so constants migrate to the inner position where constfold can attack them. Requires the intermediate result to have only one use (the outer add); otherwise reassociation would change values seen elsewhere.

passes.name: reassoc_mul
passes.doc: (a * b) * c → a * (b * c). Multiplication is associative.

passes.name: reassoc_and
passes.doc: (a & b) & c → a & (b & c). Bitwise AND is associative.

passes.name: reassoc_or
passes.doc: (a | b) | c → a | (b | c). Bitwise OR is associative.

passes.name: reassoc_xor
passes.doc: (a ^ b) ^ c → a ^ (b ^ c). Bitwise XOR is associative.

passes.name: constfold_icmp_eq
passes.doc: icmp eq c1, c2 → 1 if c1 == c2 else 0. Comparison of two integer constants folds to an i1 constant.

passes.name: constfold_icmp_ne
passes.doc: icmp ne c1, c2 → 1 if c1 != c2 else 0.

passes.name: constfold_icmp_slt
passes.doc: icmp slt c1, c2 → 1 if c1 < c2 else 0 (signed compare).

passes.name: constfold_icmp_sle
passes.doc: icmp sle c1, c2 → 1 if c1 <= c2 else 0 (signed compare).

passes.name: constfold_icmp_sgt
passes.doc: icmp sgt c1, c2 → 1 if c1 > c2 else 0 (signed compare). Reduces to lt with operands swapped.

passes.name: constfold_icmp_sge
passes.doc: icmp sge c1, c2 → 1 if c1 >= c2 else 0 (signed compare). Reduces to le with operands swapped.

passes.name: identity_icmp_eq_self
passes.doc: icmp eq X, X → 1. Equality of a value with itself is always true.

passes.name: identity_icmp_ne_self
passes.doc: icmp ne X, X → 0. A value is never not-equal to itself.

passes.name: select_true_cond
passes.doc: select 1, a, b → a. When the condition is statically true, the select's result is the true branch — no need for the instruction.

passes.name: select_false_cond
passes.doc: select 0, a, b → b. When the condition is statically false, the select's result is the false branch.

passes.name: select_same_branches
passes.doc: select c, X, X → X. When both branches are the same SSA value, the condition doesn't matter — algebraic identity.

passes.name: constfold_sdiv
passes.doc: sdiv c1, c2 → c1 / c2 (truncated toward zero). UB-PRESERVING: the where-clause REJECTS divisor == 0. LLVM's `sdiv` is undefined when the divisor is 0, so a folding pass that produced any value (including 0) for that case would replace defined-but-trapping behaviour with a concrete value, changing program semantics. We refuse to fire — the trap stays in the runtime where it belongs.

passes.name: constfold_srem
passes.doc: srem c1, c2 → c1 % c2 (sign follows dividend). UB-PRESERVING: same divisor-zero gate as sdiv.

passes.name: identity_sdiv_one_right
passes.doc: sdiv X, 1 → X. Dividing by 1 is the identity.

passes.name: dce_sdiv
passes.doc: Pure sdiv with no uses → delete. NOTE: even though sdiv can trap (div-by-zero is UB), the LLVM model considers an unobserved trap unobservable — if no instruction reads the result, the trap can be silently removed too. (Real LLVM is more conservative here in some modes; ours follows the IR's nominal semantics.)

passes.name: dce_srem
passes.doc: Pure srem with no uses → delete.

passes.name: fold_br_cond_true
passes.doc: br_cond with statically-true cond → unconditional br to the true target. Eliminates the cond operand and the false target — the false branch becomes unreachable, set up for subsequent dead-block elimination.

passes.name: fold_br_cond_false
passes.doc: br_cond with statically-false cond → unconditional br to the false target.

passes.name: eliminate_unreachable_bb
passes.doc: A basic block with no incoming branch references (not even from an unconditional br or a br_cond's true/false target edge) is unreachable. Delete it. The entry block — marked is_entry=true at parse time — is exempt: its reachability is the function's entry-point contract, not encoded by an edge.
